title: How agent o11y differs from traditional o11y — Phil Hetzel, Braintrust
talk_summary: Phil Hetzel of Braintrust argues agent observability differs from traditional o11y because agent traces are non-deterministic, huge (up to 1GB traces, 20MB spans), semi-structured with unstructured text needing full-text indexing, and consumed by both technical and non-technical people. He frames evals and observability as the same problem (batch with known inputs vs real-time with unknown inputs), and describes using lightweight LLM embedding+clustering over production traces to surface intents, sentiment, and failure modes.

takeaways.technique: Treat observability and evals as one system
takeaways.what_they_do: Same trace store feeds both real-time production monitoring and batch evals; a production trace is added to an offline dataset to experiment on.
takeaways.evidence_quote: observability and evals to us it's like we solve it with the same system. The only difference is that with evals we know the inputs ahead of time

takeaways.technique: Human/expert annotation with justifications to seed automated scorers
takeaways.what_they_do: Experts grade traces and write why; those justifications are then run through an LLM to build scalable scoring functions that encode discovered failure modes.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you're going to take those justifications, you're going to probably run an LLM over it, and you're going to make more um scalable scoring functions

takeaways.technique: LLM clustering of production traces for unknown-unknowns
takeaways.what_they_do: Run a lightweight LLM over incoming traces to embed and cluster them, doing topic modeling to surface user intent, sentiment, and recurring issues.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we'll run like a very lightweight LLM on top of them to perform embedding and then clustering on those traces

takeaways.technique: Full-text index over traces, not just metrics
takeaways.evidence_quote: it's really hard to do that unless you perform a a full text-based index across your traces
takeaways.numbers: traces up to 1GB; individual spans up to 20MB

takeaways.what_they_do: Best agent teams include non-technical domain experts (clinicians, lawyers) reviewing traces and improving prompts in natural language.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the best teams that are building agent have both technical and non-technical people in the fold performing this work
